exposure: trophectoderm (TE) biopsy of blastocysts for a PGT (Preimplantation Genetic Test)
outcome: serum b-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels 14 days after transfer
cohort: The study included pregnant women undergoing the transfer of single vitrified-warmed blastocysts, divided into a group that received preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) with trophectoderm biopsy and a control group without PGT.
finding: Trophectoderm biopsy of blastocysts for PGT did not significantly affect serum b-hCG levels 14 days after transfer, nor did it impact clinical, ongoing, or live birth pregnancy rates.
